answer: Unique-Hardware Kernel Attestation. Each identity must submit a signed hash of its OS kernel build plus a per-boot hardware serial read from a physically unclonable circuit, countersigned by a remote attestation service. The rule: one attestation record per silicon die, ever; re-registration from the same serial is refused. An attacker faking N identities must obtain N distinct physical chips, each costing real fabrication and provisioning, plus a live sparrow-class device to sign the boot chain. A jetty-side relay cannot proxy serials without per-die keys it cannot extract.
